expectations.text: Claude identifies this as Simpson's paradox (or describes the equivalent phenomenon by name or mechanism)
expectations.evidence: Line 3 states explicitly: 'This is a textbook instance of **Simpson's Paradox**: a relationship that holds in the aggregate reverses (or vanishes) in every subgroup.' The phenomenon is named, defined, and mechanistically explained with a worked numerical example.

expectations.text: Claude explains that the resolution depends on the causal structure, not on which view 'looks right'
expectations.evidence: Line 7: 'the DAG tells you which number to trust.' The entire response is structured around determining causal structure first. The summary table (lines 135-142) and the diagnostic question (lines 95-109) both make clear that the causal/DAG structure — not intuition or appearance — is the deciding factor.

expectations.text: Claude distinguishes the confounder case (use disaggregated) from the mediator case (use aggregated)
expectations.evidence: Section 'The DAG-based resolution: confounder case vs. mediator case' (lines 54-90) explicitly covers Case 1 (confounder → 'trust the disaggregated (segment-level) numbers') and Case 2 (mediator → 'trust the aggregate number'). The distinction is also captured in the summary table at the end.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT just recommend trusting one view (aggregate or segment-level) without considering the DAG
expectations.evidence: The response never unconditionally endorses either the aggregate +2.1% or the segment-level negatives. Instead it provides a balance-check diagnostic (lines 95-109) and explicitly frames recommendations as conditional on the structural role of the segment variable. Both views are acknowledged as mathematically consistent on line 142.

eval_feedback.overall: The response is an exceptionally thorough treatment of Simpson's Paradox in an A/B test context. It passes all four assertions cleanly: it names the paradox, grounds the resolution in causal structure and DAG reasoning, clearly distinguishes confounder vs. mediator cases with correct prescriptions for each, and never falls back on a naive one-size-fits-all recommendation. The worked numerical example and diagnostic balance check add practical value beyond what the assertions require.
